input.question: For walking forward in Elden Ring, do you want to tilt the physical joystick forward, or use a mouth action that keeps you moving once triggered?

options.label: Triple puff to start walking forward, keeps going until you stop it — how you moved in 47% of your other games (e.g. 007 First Light)
Tilt the joystick forward, like a normal analog stick — how you moved in 35% of your other games (e.g. Flight Simulator)
Left-center puff, held to keep moving — used in GTA V FiveM

input.question: For walking backward in Elden Ring, do you want to tilt the joystick back, or use a mouth action toggle?

options.label: Left-center sip toggles walking backward on/off — how you moved in 49% of your other games (e.g. 007 First Light)
Tilt the joystick back, like a normal analog stick — how you moved in 33% of your other games (e.g. Flight Simulator)
Left-center sip held to move backward — used in GTA V FiveM

input.question: For your regular attack (the button you'll press the most in this game), which mouth action do you want to use?

options.label: Right sip, with a short 75ms delay before it fires — used in Apex Legends
A gentle center sip fires it right away — used in Battlefield 6
Right-center puff fires it right away — used in the Default Shooter profile

input.why: Their most common pattern for L3-click jobs like crouch/stand: 17 of 35 games (49%, e.g. Apex) use a triple-puff held 500ms-16000ms. A long-hold requirement also avoids clashing with quicker triple-puff taps used elsewhere.

For R3-click jobs (reset camera/lock-on), 13 of 32 games (41%, e.g. Battlefield 2042) use a quick right-center-sip tap at 200ms; a further 16% use the same sip with a 250ms tap, so this action is their consistent default for this job.

For strong/charged attack jobs, center-puff (normal or soft) covers roughly half their game history (27% + 20%, e.g. 007 First Light, Battlefield 2042); the competing 'up' option comes from vehicle-throttle contexts, not a combat job, so it isn't a real match here.
For guard/block jobs, 15 of 39 games (38%, e.g. Apex) use a right-puff with a 100ms delay before it engages, well ahead of any other pattern.
For weapon-skill/ability jobs, 19 of 41 games (46%, e.g. ARC Raiders) use a center-sip toggle, their clear default for this kind of held/activated ability.
For dodge/dash jobs, 14 of 37 games (38%, e.g. ARC Raiders) use a plain triple-sip, clearly ahead of the next pattern (14%).
For use-item jobs, 13 of 34 games (38%, e.g. ARC Raiders) use a soft right-sip with a 250ms delay-off, their strongest single pattern for this job.
For interact/pick-up jobs, 14 of 35 games (40%, e.g. 007 First Light) use a plain soft triple-sip, well ahead of the next pattern (17%).

For switch-left-item jobs their history is split fairly evenly, but the mouth-action pattern (left-sip, 200ms delay-on) ties for the top spot and fits a mouth-operated device better than the 'W' hat-switch token seen in Eurotruck Simulator.
For switch-right-item jobs, 12 of 33 games (36%, e.g. ARC Raiders) use a plain soft left-sip, clearly their most common pattern.
For switch-spell jobs, 12 of 28 games (43%, e.g. Apex) use a soft right-center-sip tapped at 250ms, well ahead of any other pattern.
For switch-item jobs, 8 of 30 games (27%, e.g. CoD Black Ops 6) use a soft right-puff with a 250ms delay-on, their leading pattern for this job.
For open-main-menu jobs, 13 of 33 games (39%, e.g. 007 First Light) use a plain soft left-puff, ahead of the next pattern (24%, same input with a delay).

For open-map jobs, 7 of 32 games (22%, e.g. Battlefield 6) use a soft right-sip with a long 2500ms delay-off, their leading pattern; the other three options are tied at 16% each with a different input.

input.summary: Settled 14 controller-style controls by majority pattern from their other profiles (all marked inferred, since this is a first Elden Ring profile with no prior Elden Ring history to call evidenced). Left the 13 keyboard/mouse controls unbound as they have no function in this controller-style profile. Asked 3 questions where their history genuinely splits between two different ways of playing that matter for this game: moving forward, moving backward, and the main attack button, all core to real-time combat and worth their own call.
